question: Can a small neural regressor trained on model-dependent scattering simulations recover the model-independent finite-volume mapping represented by numerical Luescher quantization?

key_findings.claim: A small feed-forward network maps sampled phase-shift curves and box size to the ten lowest finite-volume energy levels.
key_findings.evidence: Training uses 2,500 parameter draws each from broad model A and sharp model C HEFT families, 100 phase-shift samples, seven lattice sizes, SoftPlus activations, and 28,362 parameters; intermediate model B is held out.

key_findings.claim: Predictions track Luescher curves across the held-out interaction family more closely than its finite-volume spectra do.
key_findings.evidence: Model-B residuals are systematically biased because the network suppresses model-specific finite-range corrections and moves spectra toward the universal numerical quantization curve; model C converges toward the curve as volume increases.

key_findings.claim: A constant-phase stress test exposes a discontinuity that the continuous network cannot represent until output labeling is manually changed.
key_findings.evidence: When phase crosses zero, a new lowest level appears and predictions zigzag; redefining level indices using sign and free-energy conventions and retraining yields strong agreement, while residual error remains near plus/minus 180 degrees.

method.core_idea: Use out-of-family generalization across HEFT potential shapes to identify the common phase-shift-to-finite-volume-spectrum mapping.
method.mechanism: A multi-branch fully connected SoftPlus network receives a 100-point phase-shift function and lattice size and regresses ordered energy levels; broad and sharp potential families train it while an intermediate family tests universality.
assumptions: The three HEFT form-factor families span enough model dependence to isolate a universal relation.
Generalization toward Luescher's known curve demonstrates rediscovery rather than interpolation.
Manually imposed energy-level conventions do not inject material prior knowledge of the target formula.

techniques.role: Tests whether the model learns common rather than family-specific finite-volume behavior.
Represents the continuous scattering relation through 100 energy samples.
Probes far outside the resonance-like training distribution and reveals output-topology failure.

evaluations.setting: HEFT models A/C training and model B test across L=10-13 fm
evaluations.metric: Energy residual distributions and phase-energy curves
evaluations.result: Residuals cluster near zero; test predictions follow Luescher curves while discarding some held-out finite-range bias.
evaluations.baseline: Direct HEFT spectra and known numerical Luescher formula

evaluations.setting: Increasing finite volume for sharp model C
evaluations.result: Both simulated data and learned relation move closer to the model-independent curve as expected finite-volume corrections shrink.

evaluations.setting: Constant phase shift from -180 to 180 degrees
evaluations.result: Initial network fails at the branch discontinuity; revised output indexing restores close agreement except near period edges.

limitations: The target Luescher relation is already known and used for validation; the network outputs no human-readable equation or proof.
All training data are synthetic HEFT calculations from three hand-designed one-channel S-wave potential families at large boxes.
A human-designed branch/index convention is required after the main OOD stress test exposes a topological discontinuity.
failure_modes: Continuous ordered-output regression smooths across energy-level births or permutations.
The network can mistake shared simulator artifacts for universal physics when training families are insufficiently diverse.
Coupled channels, partial-wave mixing, smaller volumes, and three-body spectra may lie far outside the learned map.
reusable_insights: Scientific rediscovery needs held-out mechanism families, not only random parameter splits.
Stress tests should include topology and branch changes outside smooth training regimes.
A black-box numerical surrogate is evidence of a shared relation but not a symbolic law or model-independence proof.
open_questions: Can equivariant set outputs handle energy-level permutations and births without manual indexing?
Will the approach generalize across coupled channels and three-body finite-volume formalisms?
Can symbolic distillation recover an interpretable quantization condition with uncertainty and dimensional constraints?

competitive_landscape.title: AI Feynman: a Physics-Inspired Method for Symbolic Regression
competitive_landscape.difference: AI Feynman searches for explicit symbolic expressions using physics-inspired decomposition; this work learns a black-box numerical functional beyond elementary expressions and tests cross-model universality.

competitive_landscape.title: AI Poincare: Machine Learning Conservation Laws from Trajectories
competitive_landscape.difference: AI Poincare infers conserved latent dimensions from trajectories; this paper learns a finite-volume scattering map from paired phase shifts and spectra.

competitive_landscape.title: Model independent analysis of coupled-channel scattering: a deep learning approach
competitive_landscape.difference: Sombillo et al. classify analytic pole structures from amplitudes in coupled channels; the reviewed work regresses finite-volume energy levels and asks whether cross-potential generalization reproduces Luescher quantization.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: symbolic law discovery and ML scattering analysis predate this study. Its distinct demonstration is a cross-potential neural surrogate that numerically approaches the known universal Luescher map and exposes branch-indexing as a concrete obstacle to automated discovery.
reviewer_notes: All eight pages, HEFT construction, training distribution, residual analysis, constant-phase test, manual level convention, and conclusion were checked. Primary competitor records checked 2026-08-23. 'Rediscovery' is numerical functional approximation, not an autonomous derivation.
